subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Framing Effect in Advertising
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Framing Effect in Advertising.

hook.text: Ground beef labeled 75% lean outsells the same beef labeled 25% fat. Same meat, different frame, different sales.

buildup.text: Framing shifts attention. Lean highlights the positive; fat highlights the negative. The frame decides the feeling.

discovery.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed that framing changes risk preferences. A 90% survival rate sounds better than a 10% death.

twist.text: Ethical marketers can frame honestly. Choosing which true fact to lead with is framing. All communication is framed.

climax.text: When any claim sounds great, reframe it in the opposite direction. If it still sounds great, the product is genuine.

punchline.text: The fact didn't change. The frame did.

quiz.question: Why does 75% lean outsell 25% fat beef?
options: Lean beef is actually higher quality
The positive frame shifts attention toward the desirable attribute
